newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta index ends up on fresh buying, off high.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta index ends up on fresh buying, off high.

text.p: Jakarta shares ended higher on Wednesday on fresh buying but ended the day below earlier highs after profit taking in many counters, brokers said.
They said both foreign and local investors were buying actively in several big-capitalised stocks and secondaries and this lifted the market's overall sentiment.

The Jakarta Composite Index rose 5.65 points, or 0.91 percent, to close at 629.45 points after earlier touching a high of 630.60 points. Gainers led losers by 59 to 56, with 49 counters unchanged, with total volume reaching 163.5 milllion shares worth 363.2 billion rupiah.
They said positive sentiment was due more to the rise of Indonesian stocks in New York rather than the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates unchanged.
Brokers said the market was likely to continue its positive sentiment on Thursday with possible follow-through buying on some counters.
"The market's overall sentiment is quite firm with further rises in Telkom helping to push up the index," a broker with a London-based securities house said.
Brokers said targets for both local and overseas buyers included Telkom, Indosat, Citra Marga and cigarette firms Gudang Garam and Sampoerna.

Telecommunations firm Telkom rose 125 rupiah to 4,075 rupiah on a volume of 3.5 million shares on what brokers said was fresh buying which was boosted by its higher closing price in New York last night.
"I did not hear any special news about Telkom, I believe it's really fresh buying on its fundamentals," a local broker said.
Another telecommunications firm Indosat also recorded a significant rise on what brokers said was fresh buying.
They said the movement was linked to an analysts meeting held by the company on Tuesday where it discussed the impact of changes in the accounting of its telephone revenue.
Toll road operator Citra Marga rose 50 rupiah to 1,950 rupiah, after earlier touching 1,975 rupiah, on a turnover 1.7 million shares.
An analysts' meeting called by the company boosted morning sentiment, but operators later took profits, brokers said.
The company projected a net profit of 145 billion rupiah for 1997, compared with an expected profit of 123 billion this year.
Analysts said the figures were within their expectations.
